::: {.callout-warning}
## Prototype

ISMIP8 does not exist. This page shows how the input data of an ISMIP protocol could be
distributed with FesmData. `list`, `fetch`, `mirror`, `remap` and `cite` exist today for the
FesmData datasets (see [Download](download.qmd) and [Your own data](remap.qmd)), as do
the products named below (Topo, Regions, GHF, Ocean, SMB). Proposed, and not implemented:
the bundle `ISMIP8` and its experiments, the dataset of ESM anomalies, remapping onto a
grid file (`--to`), the options `--years` and `check`. The ESMs, scenarios and the sizes
of the anomalies are illustrative.
:::

## In short

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData.git && cd FesmData
git checkout ismip8-v1.0.0                       # protocol version
julia fesmdata.jl fetch ISMIP8 Antarctica init   # common fields
julia fesmdata.jl fetch ISMIP8 Antarctica CESM2-WACCM-ssp585
julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap ISMIP8 Antarctica --to=grid_MYMODEL-10KM.txt
```

This gives every input of the experiment on your own grid, in
`$FESMDATA/Antarctica/MYMODEL-10KM/`, each file with the protocol version and the
checksums of the files it was made from. You need [Julia](https://julialang.org/downloads/)
only; `remap` installs its packages on first use. Set `FESMDATA` to the folder for the data
(see [Download](download.qmd#where-the-data-go)).

## How it works

The ISMIP forcing comes from many ESMs and scenarios, with each field every year, so the
full set of files on the ISMIP grids reaches terabytes. Most groups then interpolate it
onto their own grid anyway. Here, each input is stored once, on a **reference grid** no
finer than the information it holds, and remapped on your machine onto the grid you run:

- the fields that are the same in all experiments (topography, basins, the ocean and SMB
  climatologies) are fine, small and stored once, on fine grids;
- the anomalies from the ESMs, which make up nearly all of the volume, are stored on
  coarse grids (8 to 32 km), since an ESM (or a regional model at 10 km) holds no finer
  structure.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S["ESM output,<br/>observations,<br/>regional models"] -->|"ISMIP team:<br/>prepare, remap"| R[("Reference files<br/>on reference grids<br/>versioned, sha256")]
  R -->|"fetch"| L["$FESMDATA<br/>on your machine"]
  L -->|"remap --to=your grid"| M["Inputs on your grid,<br/>with provenance"]
  R -.->|"mirror"| H["Shared copy on<br/>an HPC system"]
  H -.->|"remap"| M
```

What is fetched, and how each input is remapped (method, smoothing, how anomalies are
combined with climatologies), is fixed by the protocol, in a file under version control
(see [Setting up a protocol](#setting-up-a-protocol)). All groups thus get the same inputs
from the same files by the same method, whatever their grid, and each file records how it
was made.

## What ISMIP8 contains

`julia fesmdata.jl list ISMIP8` shows the members, the experiments and their sizes. Each
member is a product of a FesmData dataset, from any theme; the anomalies of the ESMs are
the products of the dataset `ISMIP8`.

**Antarctica**

| Member | Product | Source | Reference grid | Remapping | Size |
|----------|------------------------|---------|---------|----------|--------|
| geometry | TOPO-BedMachine-v4 | 500 m | ANT-1KM | con | 228 MB |
| basins | BASINS-IMBIE2016 | polygons | ANT-1KM | class | 1 MB |
| ghf | GHF-Stal2020 | 20 km | ANT-16KM | con, smooth | 0.1 MB |
| ocean-climatology | Ocean-ISMIP7 | 8 km | ANT-8KM | con, smooth | 26 MB |
| smb-climatology | SMB-RACMO2.4p1-1991-2020 | 11 km | ANT-8KM | con, smooth | 3 MB |
| ocean | ISMIP8-ocean-*ESM*-*scenario* | ESM, about 1° | ANT-32KM | con, smooth, + climatology | 5.9 GB each |
| atmosphere | ISMIP8-atmosphere-*ESM*-*scenario* | ESM, about 1° | ANT-32KM | con, smooth | 0.26 GB each |

**Greenland**

| Member | Product | Source | Reference grid | Remapping | Size |
|----------|------------------------|---------|---------|----------|--------|
| geometry | TOPO-BedMachine-v6 | 150 m | GRL-1KM | con | 35 MB |
| basins | BASINS-Mouginot2019 | polygons | GRL-1KM | class | 0.1 MB |
| ghf | GHF-Colgan2021 | 55 km | GRL-32KM | con, smooth | 0.03 MB |
| smb-climatology | SMB-MARv3.14-1991-2020 | 10 km | GRL-8KM | con, smooth | 0.6 MB |
| atmosphere | ISMIP8-atmosphere-*ESM*-*scenario* | MAR, 10 km | GRL-8KM | con, smooth | 0.55 GB each |
| ocean | ISMIP8-ocean-*ESM*-*scenario* | by basin | by basin | value of the basin | < 1 MB each |

The products come from the datasets Topo, Regions (`BASINS-`), GHF, Ocean, SMB and
ISMIP8. The anomalies are, in Antarctica, of temperature, salinity and thermal forcing on
30 levels (ocean) and of the SMB and surface temperature with their elevation gradients
(atmosphere: aSMB, dSMBdz, aST, dSTdz), annual, 1850-2300; in Greenland, the same
atmosphere fields from MAR, and the thermal forcing and runoff of each basin (ocean).
Remapping: `con` conservative; `smooth` Gaussian smoothing where the reference grid is
coarser than yours; `class` the dominant class of each cell; `+ climatology` added to the
ocean climatology.

The reference grid of a member is the coarsest FesmData grid at least as fine as its
source, and no finer than the finest grid of the ISMIP8 models (1 km). ANT-8KM is the
ISMIP 8 km grid (761 × 761 cells, EPSG:3031). The sizes of the anomalies are uncompressed;
the others are those of the released files.

**Experiments.** The names given to `fetch` and `remap` select the members:

| Name | Members |
|---|---|
| `init` | geometry, basins, ghf and the climatologies: the fields common to all experiments |
| `<ESM>-<scenario>` | `init` and the anomalies of one ESM and scenario (historical to 2014), e.g. `CESM2-WACCM-ssp585` |
| `tier1` | `init` and the 6 Tier 1 pairs: CESM2-WACCM, UKESM1-0-LL and MRI-ESM2-0 under ssp126 and ssp585 |
| `tier2` | `init` and the 12 Tier 2 pairs: IPSL-CM6A-LR, NorESM2-MM and ACCESS-ESM1-5 under all three scenarios, and the Tier 1 ESMs under ssp245 |
| `all` | everything |

## Get the reference files

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl list ISMIP8                          # members, experiments, sizes
julia fesmdata.jl list ISMIP8 Antarctica tier1         # files, sizes, which are here
julia fesmdata.jl fetch ISMIP8 Antarctica tier1        # download and verify (sha256)
julia fesmdata.jl fetch ISMIP8 Greenland all
```

Files go to `$FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/`, the reference grid of each member, and are
checked against their checksums. Files already present are kept if they are of the
release (e.g. Topo, fetched for another purpose), and updated if they are of an earlier
one.

On the HPC systems used by several groups, one copy is kept up to date with
`julia fesmdata.jl mirror ISMIP8`, and each group sets `FESMDATA` to it: nothing is
downloaded, only remapped.

## Remap onto your grid

```bash
julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap ISMIP8 Antarctica tier1 --to=grid_MYMODEL-10KM.txt
julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap ISMIP8 Antarctica CESM2-WACCM-ssp585 ANT-16KM
```

The target is either your own grid, given by a grid file (`--to`), or a FesmData grid
(`ANT-16KM`; see [Domains and grids](domains.qmd)). A grid file is either a grid
description of cdo, as the FesmData grid files `grid_<GRID>.txt`, or a NetCDF file with the
coordinates `x`, `y` and a grid mapping (polar stereographic, as for the ISMIP grids). The
grid is named after the file (`MYMODEL-10KM`), and the files are written to
`$FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<product>.nc`.

Each member is remapped as the protocol says (conservatively, then smoothed where the
reference grid is coarser than yours; classes by dominant class), slice by slice for the
fields with time and depth. The ocean anomalies are added to the climatology on your
grid, so the ocean files hold the full fields, as in ISMIP6; the atmosphere anomalies
stay anomalies, applied by your model with its own surface elevation (dSMBdz, dSTdz).

The remapped files are as large as your grid makes them: the ocean forcing of one ESM and
scenario is 6 GB on ANT-32KM, but 94 GB on ANT-8KM and 375 GB on ANT-4KM (uncompressed).
Select what you run:

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl remap ISMIP8 Antarctica CESM2-WACCM-ssp585 \
    --to=grid_MYMODEL-4KM.txt --vars=tf --years=1995:2300
```

If your model interpolates its forcing at run time, use the reference files as they are
(`julia fesmdata.jl path ISMIP8 Antarctica CESM2-WACCM-ssp585`).

## What you get

```
$FESMDATA/Antarctica/
  ANT-32KM/                                    reference files (fetch)
    ANT-32KM_ISMIP8-ocean-CESM2-WACCM-ssp585.nc
    ANT-32KM_ISMIP8-atmosphere-CESM2-WACCM-ssp585.nc
  ANT-8KM/
    ANT-8KM_Ocean-ISMIP7.nc
    ...
  MYMODEL-10KM/                                your grid (remap)
    grid_MYMODEL-10KM.txt
    MYMODEL-10KM_grid.nc                       x, y, lon, lat, area of the cells
    MYMODEL-10KM_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc
    MYMODEL-10KM_BASINS-IMBIE2016.nc
    MYMODEL-10KM_ISMIP8-ocean-CESM2-WACCM-ssp585.nc
    MYMODEL-10KM_ISMIP8-atmosphere-CESM2-WACCM-ssp585.nc
    ...
    ISMIP8_inputs.toml                         the inputs used, for your submission
```

Each file records how it was made in its global attributes, e.g.:

```
ismip_protocol   = "ismip8-v1.0.0"
source_files     = "ANT-8KM_Ocean-ISMIP7.nc, ANT-32KM_ISMIP8-ocean-CESM2-WACCM-ssp585.nc"
source_checksums = "sha256:3f9c...e1, sha256:a41e...07"
remap_method     = "conservative, then Gaussian smoothing (sigma = 16.0 km)"
fesmdata_commit  = "8b39427"
```

`julia fesmdata.jl check ISMIP8 MYMODEL-10KM` checks the files on your grid against the
protocol (version, checksums of the reference files, methods) and writes
`ISMIP8_inputs.toml`, the list of the inputs used, to submit with your model output. ISMIP
can then confirm that all groups ran with the same forcing.

## Why reference grids

The forcing of one ESM and scenario (uncompressed, annual 1850-2300):

| | On the ISMIP grids | On the reference grids |
|---|---|---|
| Antarctica, ocean (T, S, TF; 30 levels) | 94 GB (ANT-8KM) | 5.9 GB (ANT-32KM) |
| Antarctica, atmosphere (4 fields) | 4.2 GB (ANT-8KM) | 0.26 GB (ANT-32KM) |
| Greenland, atmosphere (4 fields, MAR at 10 km) | 35 GB (GRL-1KM) | 0.55 GB (GRL-8KM) |
| One ESM and scenario | 133 GB | 6.7 GB |
| 18 ESMs and scenarios | 2.4 TB | 121 GB |

The factor of 20 comes from the cells alone: 16 times fewer from 8 to 32 km, 64 times fewer
from 1 to 8 km. Compression reduces both by a similar factor; the released FesmData files
show it, e.g. the annual RACMO2.4p1 SMB (1979-2023) is 23 MB on ANT-8KM and 2.3 MB on
ANT-32KM, and the ISMIP7 ocean climatology 26 MB and 2.4 MB.

Remapping twice (from the source to the reference grid, then to yours) adds little error
as long as the reference grid is at least as fine as the source: both steps are
conservative, and the smoothing only removes the steps between the coarse cells. Each
release checks this (step 3 under [Setting up a protocol](#setting-up-a-protocol)).

## Setting up a protocol {#setting-up-a-protocol}

*For the ISMIP team.* A protocol is a folder of FesmData and the products it refers to:

```
FesmData/
  ISMIP8/
    bundle.toml                  members, reference grids, remapping, experiments
    README.md                    this page
    prepare.jl                   ESM output -> prepared anomalies (or the ISMIP tools)
  registry/Antarctica/ISMIP8.toml    uri and sha256 of each reference file (by release)
  registry/Greenland/ISMIP8.toml
```

`bundle.toml` defines what `fetch ISMIP8` and `remap ISMIP8` mean:

```toml
[members.geometry]
product = "Topo/TOPO-BedMachine-v4"
grids = { Antarctica = 1 }                    # reference grid (km)
remap = { method = "con" }

[members.ocean-climatology]
product = "Ocean/Ocean-ISMIP7"
grids = { Antarctica = 8 }
remap = { method = "con", smooth = "auto" }

[members.ocean]
product = "ISMIP8/ISMIP8-ocean-{esm}-{scenario}"
grids = { Antarctica = 32 }
remap = { method = "con", smooth = "auto", add_to = "ocean-climatology" }

[experiments]
init  = ["geometry", "basins", "ghf", "ocean-climatology", "smb-climatology"]
tier1 = { esm = ["CESM2-WACCM", "UKESM1-0-LL", "MRI-ESM2-0"], scenario = ["ssp126", "ssp585"] }
```

The steps of a release:

1. **Prepare** the output of each ESM and scenario with the ISMIP tools (e.g. the
   extrapolation into the ice-shelf cavities), as prepared files: NetCDF on the native or
   ISMIP grid, with units and references (see [Your own data](remap.qmd)).
2. **Remap** them onto the reference grids: `julia fesmdata.jl remap ISMIP8`.
3. **Verify** the reference grids: remapped from the reference grid onto the ISMIP grid,
   each field must match the field remapped from the source within a tolerance (e.g.
   0.05 °C in thermal forcing).
4. **Release**: `stamp` and `release` upload the files and write their uri and checksum
   to the registry; commit and tag `ismip8-v1.0.0`.

The registry holds only addresses and checksums, so the files can stay where ISMIP keeps
them now (e.g. the public HTTPS of the ISMIP Globus endpoint), with copies on Helmholtz
Codebase or Zenodo (a DOI per release). An erratum is a patch release (`ismip8-v1.0.1`):
`julia fesmdata.jl list ISMIP8 --outdated` shows each group the files that changed, and
`fetch` and `remap` replace only those.

The protocol can also add steps of its own after remapping, as Julia functions in
`ISMIP8/`: adding anomalies to a climatology (`add_to`), extrapolating ocean fields into
the cavities of the model's own ice mask, or computing the thermal forcing at the model's
depths. The bundle is generic: another intercomparison (e.g. a PMIP or a regional MIP)
would be another folder with its own `bundle.toml`, using the same products.
